title: Plausible vs DataFast
description: Plausible vs DataFast — compare privacy-first web analytics vs revenue attribution for Stripe SaaS and indie products.
verdict: Plausible is built for simple, privacy-first traffic analytics on marketing sites and blogs. DataFast covers similar lightweight web analytics but adds optional payment-processor revenue attribution so indie SaaS teams can see which channels drive paid customers — not just pageviews.
quickAnswer: **Plausible** is the better fit if you need **clean, cookieless traffic reports** without payment wiring. **DataFast** is the better fit if your north star is **revenue per channel** for a Stripe (or similar) product and you can pass visitor IDs into checkout metadata.
bottomLine: Choose **Plausible** for privacy-first marketing analytics with a mature open-source/self-host option and pageview-tier pricing from $9/month. Choose **DataFast** when "which landing page made money?" matters more than a pure privacy pageview dashboard. Content sites with no checkout should default to Plausible (or Fathom); paid SaaS with short online checkout paths should strongly consider DataFast.

faq.question: Can Plausible do revenue attribution like DataFast?
faq.answer: Not out of the box. Plausible can track goals and custom events, but it does not offer DataFast-style Stripe (and similar) revenue-per-channel reports. You would need custom events plus your own join logic.

faq.question: Can DataFast replace Plausible for simple traffic stats?
faq.answer: Yes for many indie SaaS marketing sites. DataFast includes pageviews, referrers, and goals. Skip revenue attribution if you only need traffic — but if you never connect payments, Plausible or Fathom may be a clearer privacy-first fit.

faq.question: Which is more privacy-friendly?
faq.answer: Both position as privacy-friendly alternatives to GA4. Plausible is widely chosen for cookieless, EU-oriented marketing analytics. DataFast’s default mode uses first-party cookies for multi-day journeys and revenue matching; cookieless mode is available with weaker attribution. Confirm consent needs with counsel either way.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: Plausible starts at $9/month for 10K pageviews. DataFast Starter is in a similar entry range for small products — compare your pageviews and whether you need revenue features in our pricing calculator.

faq.question: Can either be self-hosted?
faq.answer: Plausible offers an open-source self-hosted edition. DataFast is cloud-only SaaS.

editorialNotes.title: Different primary questions
editorialNotes.content: Plausible answers "where did traffic come from and which pages convert to goals?" DataFast answers that plus "which channel led to **paid** customers?" If you do not have online payments, DataFast’s differentiator is unused — pick Plausible or Fathom instead.

editorialNotes.title: Script weight
editorialNotes.content: Both are lightweight vs GA4/PostHog on our recorded benches (roughly +250 ms load overhead and single-digit KiB transfer on the Slow-4G fixture). See individual benchmark pages for exact numbers.
